newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TWO-GOAL FOWLER SPEARHEADS LIVERPOOL'S VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO-GOAL FOWLER SPEARHEADS LIVERPOOL'S VICTORY.

text.p: Liverpool stayed on course to win the only European trophy to elude them when they crushed Brann Bergen 3-0 at Anfield on Thursday for a place in the semifinals of the Cup Winners' Cup.
Robbie Fowler spearheaded the victory with a goal in each half to take his total to six in the competition and 28 in all matches this season.
Substitute Stan Collymore scored the second goal in the 62nd minute, just two minutes after replacing Czech Patrick Berger, as Liverpool clinched a comprehensive 4-1 aggregate victory.

It also put the four-time European champions into the semifinal of a European competition for the first time since 1985 when they lost the European Cup final to Juventus and were then banned from Europe following the Heysel Stadium disaster in Brussels.

Although Norway's Brann, who are currently in their close-season, threatened with a couple of chances early on, once Fowler put Liverpool ahead from the penalty spot after 25 minutes, the odds were always heavily tipped Liverpool's way.

Italian referee Alfredo Trentalange immediatly pointed to the spot after Fowler appeared to be upended by both Brann skipper Claus Eftevaag and Stefan Paldan, and Fowler made no mistake from the spot.

Berger had a number of chances to increase Liverpool's lead, but wasted them all and with the fans growing impatient and calling for Collymore, Liverpool manager Roy Evans brought on his unsettled 8.5 million pounds ($13.6 million) striker for the Czech after an hour.
Collymore, who missed the away leg in Norway, wasted little time in getting his name on the scoresheet for the 14th time this season.
He forced his way through the centre of the Brann defence before getting a lucky deflection off Per Ove Ludvigsen with the ball bouncing past goalkeeper Vidar Bahus off Collymore's shin.

A sweet Liverpool move involving Steve McManaman and Norwegian Stig Inge Bjornebye set up Fowler's second 12 minutes from time, the striker giving goalkeeper Vidar Bahus no chance with an angled shot from eight metres out.
"There were a few worrying moments early on, but we played patient football which is what you need in Europe, and in the end I think we could have won by more," Evans said afterwards.
"But the crowd didn't influence me to bring Stan on. I was thinking of doing that anyway, but obviously great minds think alike," he joked.
Brann's manager Kjell Tennfjord said: "We had our chances, but Liverpool deserved their victory.
"I thought that maybe their first and second goals were lucky ones, but we had our chances too and did not take them.
"Right now we are in our close-season. If we come back in six months, maybe it will be a different story, but I think they are the best team in England, better than Manchester United."

Liverpool, who won the European Cup in 1977, 1978, 1981 and 1984, also won the UEFA Cup in 1973 and 1976. Their best performance in the Cup Winners' Cup came in 1966 when they lost the final to Borussia Dortmund after extra time at Hampden Park.
The only teams to win all three European trophies are Ajax, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Juventus. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
